observation: The leak does not form the intended sideways fan spray from the burst fitting; instead the water appears as a mostly coherent vertical stream/sheet with minimal atomization.
expected_behavior: A pressurized hose burst should emit a sideways, fanned spray pattern that hits the cabinet side wall and produces strong splash/spray at the impact plus ripples in the pooled water.
actual_behavior: Water falls mostly vertically with a smooth/laminar column; little to no fan spread, droplets, mist, or energetic impact detail. Pool reads as a flat reflective plane with weak ripples.

suspected_parameters.inflow_rotation: plane normal likely not pointing toward side wall

recommended_fix: Rotate the inflow plane so its normal points toward the left cabinet wall (sideways), then keep velocity_normal ~1.75-2.0. Enable secondary liquid particles (use_spray_particles/use_foam_particles/use_bubble_particles) to add atomization and impact detail. Increase vorticity toward 1.0 and reduce mesh smoothing (mesh_smoothen_pos/neg from 2 -> 1 or 0) to preserve ripples/breakup at resolution_max=96. Rebake ALL cache after these changes.
analysis_notes: Observed vertical/laminar jet strongly indicates emitter normal misalignment + lack of secondary particles. Pool flatness consistent with high mesh smoothing + low turbulence parameters at fixed res 96.
